details:
How It Works and What It Does

The Astra Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive educational game where children step into the role of junior astronauts exploring simulated environments like the Moon. The player manages essential life-support resources—such as water, oxygen, energy, and food—while completing mission tasks.

The game is directly anchored in real NASA space weather datasets, linking critical survival decisions (such as radiation protection) to actual environmental conditions. Key features include:

  • An AI-driven interactive mascot that users can customize using a photo.
  • Dynamic environmental hazards, such as dust storms equipped with visual freezing effects and mission timers.
  • A second-screen parental control dashboard that allows supervisors to monitor progress.
  • Visual evolution updates as items and habitats are repaired or upgraded.

Project Benefits

  • High-Quality Screen Time: Transforms low-quality recreational screen time into a productive, engaging educational experience.
  • Balanced Cognitive Load: Avoids overwhelming young players by focusing on four essential resources (oxygen, energy, food and water) rather than complex, cluttered systems.
  • Non-Punitive Replayability: Utilizes variable mechanics and events between playthroughs to encourage children to learn from failure without feeling discouraged.
  • Accessibility and Safety: Features built-in accessibility options and a parental control system to ensure a secure, inclusive environment.

Intended Impact

The primary goal of the project is to ignite early interest in STEM and space exploration, guided by the vision that "the person who will step on the moon might be taking their first steps in our game". It addresses children's feelings of isolation in digital spaces by providing meaningful, interactive companionship through AI mascots and collaborative tasks, helping shape the next generation of scientifically literate explorers.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • NASA Data & Science Datasets: Utilizes official NASA space weather data and lunar trivia to guarantee scientific traceability and verifiability.
  • Artificial Intelligence (AI): Powers the interactive companion mascot and Face ID personalization features.
  • Development Software: Built using modern web and software frameworks supporting multi-phase level design, timer progress trackers, and second-screen parental dashboards.

Creativity and Innovation

The project stands out by treating content as the primary attraction rather than relying solely on superficial visual polish. Its creative highlights include:

  • Real-World Science Integration: Tying in-game survival choices directly to live, current space weather metrics.
  • Personalized AI Companion: Enabling players to generate a custom mascot using Face ID.
  • Authentic Trade-offs: Eschewing "safe choices" that lack educational depth, ensuring every decision reflects genuine mission planning constraints.

Key Design Factors Considered

  • Simplicity and Focus: Ensuring young players are not overloaded with too many simultaneous systems.
  • Mechanical Precision: Valuing functional, accurate game mechanics over superficial visual effects.
  • Pedagogical Approach: Grounding interactions in positive reinforcement and educational frameworks.
  • Verifiable Transparency: Ensuring prototypes clearly explain which NASA datasets were used and why, making the science fully traceable for judges and educators.
